_meta.methodology_version: Method v2.0 — child-protective over-compliance (strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food ML, applied to all supplements)
method_prose: No government sets a heavy-metal maximum level for a dietary supplement that protects a child. The adult frameworks that exist — sovereign food-supplement limits (lead 1000–10000 µg/kg), USP <2232> elemental-contaminant PDEs computed for an adult consumer, California Proposition 65 warning doses — are written for a 60–70 kg adult. HMTc instead holds every supplement, adult- or child-labelled, to the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food maximum level for each analyte, because children routinely consume adult supplements (gummies, protein powders, greens, melatonin drops) and body-weight-normalised exposure makes the child the binding safety case.

Every value on this page is therefore a child-protective read-across, disclosed as such: the anchor is a real sovereign infant-food limit, named in the derivation below, applied to supplements as a voluntary over-compliance. The laxer adult floor is disclosed on every analyte and never selects the number. Where no government sets an infant-and-child-food limit for an analyte — total and hexavalent chromium, methylmercury — no number is invented: the analyte is placed under mandatory control with reflex speciation.
